channel.description: math.CA updates on the arXiv.org e-print archive.

item.title: Sharp Estimates for Jacobi Heat Kernels on a Ball and on a Simplex in the Full Range of Parameters
item.description: arXiv:2611.28330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish genuinely sharp heat-kernel estimates for orthogonal expansions on the Euclidean unit ball and on the unit simplex throughout their natural parameter ranges. For the ball weight $W_\mu(x)=(1-\|x\|^2)^{\mu-1/2}$, we extend the known estimate from the range $\mu\geq0$ to every $\mu>-1/2$. For the simplex, we prove the corresponding estimate for every $\kappa\in(-1/2,\infty)^{d+1}$. The estimates retain exactly the form known in the classical ranges. The proof is based on analytic continuation of the classical product and reduction formulas. Below the integrability threshold, the ball formula decomposes into an endpoint term and a derivative correction, while the simplex formula produces endpoint and mixed-derivative terms indexed by the negative coordinates. In the lowest simplex parameter range we use the auxiliary even ultraspherical kernel introduced by Nowak, Sj\"ogren, and Szarek.
item.dc:creator: Dawid Hanrahan

item.title: Perturbed Nevo--Thangavelu maximal functions on two-step nilpotent groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.28400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider a step-two nilpotent Lie group $G$ identified with $\mathbb R^d\times \mathbb R^m$ in exponential coordinates. We study maximal operators associated with parabolic dilates of smooth convex hypersurfaces with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature in a tilted $d$-dimensional subspace of $G$. We focus on the low-rank regime, where the rank is determined by the group law and the tilt. When $m=1$, we determine the optimal range of $p$ for which the maximal operator is bounded on $L^p(G)$. For $m\ge2$, we characterize, in terms of a {\L}ojasiewicz exponent, when the known necessary condition on $p$ is also sufficient.
item.dc:creator: Jaehyeon Ryu

item.title: Vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and boundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type
item.description: arXiv:2611.28714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In present paper, for functional-differential equations of retarded type, the method of vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and the method of higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals are developed. On the basis of this methods, sufficient conditions for various types of uniform boundedness of solutions and sufficient conditions for various types of ultimate-uniform boundedness of solutions are obtained.
item.dc:creator: K. S. Lapin, S. V. Lapin

item.title: Differential equations for Macdonald's hypergeometric series via Dunkl operators of type A
item.description: arXiv:2611.29289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve an eigenvalue problem for a family of trigonometric Dunkl operators depending on a parameter, extending the result of Ref.[16] to the case of a general parameter. We introduce families of nonsymmetric W-type operators closely related to Dunkl operators and analyze their algebraic structure, various representations and symmetrization. We then use these operators to characterize non-symmetric Macdonald's hypergeometric series introduced in Ref.[5] and recover several known results. These results suggest a direct connection between Macdonald's hypergeometric series and Dunkl operators.
item.dc:creator: Fan Liu

item.title: Qualitative WALA, Alberti representations and Lipschitz differentiability
item.description: arXiv:2611.29700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the existing theory of Lipschitz differentiability spaces implies that a metric measure space satisfying a qualitative analogue of the WALA condition of David--Semmes has many independent Alberti representations, and provides conditions for when such a space is rectifiable.
item.dc:creator: David Bate

item.title: A surprising bound for the $2\times2$ matrix weighted martingale multiplier
item.description: arXiv:2611.29784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For real $2\times2$ matrix weights, we prove that a scalar martingale multiplier on a dyadic root has $L^2(W)$ norm at most $CQ\sqrt{1+\log(Q)}$, where $Q$ is the dyadic matrix $A_2$ characteristic. A single multiplier, with signs alternating by generation, attains this order for every sufficiently large characteristic scale. We show that the restriction on the matrix size is essential: these estimates jump to the order $Q^{3/2}$ from the matrix size $3\times 3$ onward.
item.dc:creator: Komla Domelevo, Stefanie Petermichl

item.title: The dimensions of curly and dipolar Besicovitch-Kakeya sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.29803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp Hausdorff dimension and box-counting dimension bounds for sets containing meridian circles and for sets whose difference sets contain a sphere. Fix two antipodal points N, S on S^{n-1}, n\ge 3, and consider the family of great circles passing through them. Assuming the Besicovitch-Kakeya overlapping conjecture in R^{n-1}, we prove that every bounded set K\subset R^n containing a translated and dilated copy of each circle in this family satisfies \dim_H K\ge n-1. In particular, the same conclusion holds for bounded sets containing a circle in every orientation. This bound is sharp, as shown by the unit sphere. We also prove unconditionally that every bounded set K\subset R^n, n\ge2, satisfying S^{n-1}\subset K-K has lower box counting dimension greater than or equal to n(n-1)/(2n-1), and the bound is also sharp.
item.dc:creator: Antonio C\'ordoba, Chuhan Sun

item.title: On the Bourgain-Rudnick eigenfunction restriction conjecture in four dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.29806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a uniform upper $L^2$ bound for eigenfunctions of the four-dimensional flat torus on the compact paraboloid $\mathbb{P}^3$. The main novelty is the use of Fourier restriction estimates. We interpret spherical lattice point statistics as non-concentration inequalities of the strength needed to apply the Du--Zhang fractal restriction theorem. We apply their result on two-dimensional slices of $\mathbb{P}^3$. Further possible extensions are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Ciprian Demeter

item.title: Sharp constant off-diagonal extrapolation for Muckenhoupt bases
item.description: arXiv:2611.29863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we prove a sharp constant version of off-diagonal extrapolation for matrix weights, improving the result we proved in an earlier paper. In an appendix, we give a new and simpler proof of this result in the scalar case.
item.dc:creator: David Cruz-Uribe, Fatih Sirin

item.title: OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture: A harmonic analytic perspective
item.description: arXiv:2611.30274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note presents OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture. It is written for harmonic analysts who may be new to quaternionic Monge--Amp\`ere equations. We introduce the quaternionic Hessian and explain how the associated determinant equation leads to the critical annular estimate.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Wang

item.title: On the measure of Neighborhoods of Kakeya and Truncated Nikodym Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.30622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there exist Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose $\delta$-neighborhoods have measure $\lesssim |\log\delta|^{-(d-1)}$. We also show that the measure of a $\delta$-neighborhood of an $\epsilon$-truncated Nikodym set in $\mathbb{R}^2$ $\gtrsim \epsilon^{-1}|\log\delta|^{-1}$, for $\delta$ small enough. The sufficiently small scale depends on the Nikodym set and on $\epsilon$.
item.dc:creator: Iqra Altaf

item.title: The $T1$ theorem under Dini regularity
item.description: arXiv:2611.30870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the $T1$ theorem for Calder\'on-Zygmund operators under the classical Dini regularity condition on the kernel, solving a longstanding open problem in singular integral theory.
item.dc:creator: Kangwei Li

item.title: Weighted Bergman projection in radial trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.31182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Bergman projection $P_\omega $ on a radial tree with respect to weighted harmonic Bergman spaces $A^p_\omega $, where $\omega $ is a positive radial weight. We prove that for all such weights and $1<p<\infty $, the Bergman projection $P_\omega $ is bounded from $L^p(\omega) $ to $A^p_\omega $ and $L^\infty \to \mathcal{B} $, where $\mathcal{B} $ is the Bloch space of the tree. We also provide a characterization of the weights $\omega $ for which the positive Bergman projection $P_\omega^+ $ is bounded from $L^p(\omega) $ to $L^p(\omega) $. Finally, in the appendix, we provide an elementary proof of the characterization of the weights $\Omega \in L^1(\mathbb{D}) $ for which the Bergman projection from $L^p(\Omega) $ to the holomorphic Bergman space $A^p_\Omega(\mathbb{D}) $.
item.dc:creator: Nikolaos Chalmoukis, Matteo Monti

item.title: Trigonal Elliptic Coordinates on the Sphere and Some Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.28992v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a theta-function parametrization of the unit sphere adapted to the eight trigonal directions. The construction follows from a cubic theta identity discussed by Bobek and admits an equivalent representation in Jacobi elliptic functions. The angular parameter and theta nome give a nonorthogonal coordinate system whose squared Cartesian components are related to the three-component Volterra chain. An algebraic change of angle, retaining the nome, yields orthogonal coordinates with explicit metric coefficients and a diagonal Laplace--Beltrami operator. We apply both parametrizations to the geometry of O'Brien's reduced Jahn--Teller model and give compact expressions for real spherical harmonics of degrees two and three. The orthogonal angle is the polar angle of an $E_g$ quadrupolar doublet, while one octupolar harmonic depends only on the nome within each octant.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Mikhalev

item.title: Global topology and symmetry breaking in an indefinite superlinear Dirichlet problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.29550v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the work of Fencl and L\'opez-G\'omez [13] on global bifurcation diagrams, we study the connected components of positive solutions of $-u''=\lambda u+a(x)u^p$ on $(-1,1)$ with $u(-1)=u(1)=0$, where $a$ changes sign and $p\ge2$ is an integer. For generic $\mathcal C^r$ weights, $r\ge2$, with $n$ positive intervals, simple zeros and negative endpoint values, we obtain at least $2^{n-1}$ noncompact components. Apart from the principal component, each is a curve with both ends at $\lambda=-\infty$. The proof distinguishes at least $2^n-1$ ends and yields bounds for branching and compactly supported cohomology. For even weights, an odd Morse index of at least $k$ on the principal symmetric component forces at least $k$ symmetry-breaking points. In particular, symmetry breaking occurs if $a(0)<0$.
item.dc:creator: Juan Carlos Sampedro

item.title: Two-Dimensional Local Smoothing in Noncommutative Spaces and Its Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.30520v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove local smoothing for planar half-waves with coefficients in a semifinite tracial von Neumann algebra $M$. For $N\ge2$ and $P_N=\psi(|D|/N)$ with $\psi\in C_c^\infty((1/2,2))$, we obtain $\|e^{it|D|}P_N f\|_{L^4([1,2]\times\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}\le C_\psi\sqrt{\log(2+N)}\|f\|_{L^4(\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}$ uniformly in $M$ and its trace. Pairing the Dirichlet energies for $M$ and its opposite algebra cancels a determinant contribution that can have either sign. At $p=4$, summation over frequency annuli gives local smoothing for every Sobolev order $s>0$. Interpolating the annular estimates before summation gives spacetime $L^p$ bounds for $2\le p\le\infty$ and Sobolev orders $s>\sigma(p)=\max\{0,1/2-2/p\}$, as well as logarithmically weighted bounds at $s=\sigma(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$. The finite-$p$ bounds transfer to quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes, answering the question of Hong, Lai and Wang about the range $s>\sigma(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$ on generalized Moyal planes. For $1<p<\infty$ and complex $\alpha$ with $\operatorname{Re}\alpha>\max\{2/p-1,1/p-1/2,-1/p\}$, we prove maximal inequalities over all radii for generalized circular means on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes. For an action $\beta$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ on $M$ by normal trace-preserving $*$-automorphisms with norm-continuous $L^p$ orbits, the orbit mean $A_{t,\beta}^\alpha x$ converges bilaterally almost uniformly to $\pi x/\Gamma(1+\alpha)$ as $t\downarrow0$ for every $x\in L^p(M)$. We also obtain estimates for truncated cone multipliers on three-dimensional Euclidean and quantum Euclidean spaces, and full-radius row and column bounds for Stein's square function on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes.
item.dc:creator: Xudong Lai, Siyu Liu

item.title: Kinetic transfer or regularity in any dimension from uncertainty inequalities on the real line
item.description: arXiv:2611.30703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The purpose of this short note is to show that one dimensional uncertainty inequalities easily induce transfer of regularity inequalities in kinetic equations in any dimension.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Auscher (LMO)

item.title: When Positivity Matters: Maximal Distance Integrals on Curves and Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.31045v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How far apart, on average, can $n$ points in a set $A$ be? As $n\to\infty$ the answer is the $\textit{maximal energy}$ $M^{+}(A)$, the largest possible value of $\mathbb{E}|X-Y|$ when $X$ and $Y$ are independent random points of $A$ with a common distribution. If the distribution is allowed to carry negative mass, we obtain a second constant $M(A)\ge M^{+}(A)$. It is often far easier to compute: when a signed equilibrium measure exists, it is characterized by a $\textit{linear}$ potential equation, whereas the positive problem must also locate the support of the mass. This paper asks when positivity matters, that is, when $M^{+}(A)<M(A)$. For polygons and polyhedra the extremal mass sits on the vertices and closed forms abound. Even so, every hollow convex polygon has $M^{+}<M$, and a simple kite shows how a vertex can be forced out of the support. For smooth curves and surfaces the answer depends on the shape. Circles and spheres have $M^{+}=M$. The ellipse $x^2+4y^2=4$ has $M^{+}=M$ numerically, and we give its value to 50 digits. The ellipses $x^2+9y^2=9$ and $x^2+25y^2=25$ have $M^{+}<M$ numerically, with gaps in the support. For the ellipsoid $10x^2+15y^2+12z^2=15$, studied by Larcher, Schmid and Wolf, we compute 50 digits of $M$ and give strong numerical evidence that $M^{+}<M$. The extremal measure vanishes on two caps around the ends of the shortest axis. Proofs and numerical methods are collected in appendices.
item.dc:creator: Steven Finch

item.title: Rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
item.description: arXiv:2611.31075v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce and classify rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process that are solvable by polynomials. These diffusions are closely related to exceptional Hermite polynomials and rational extensions of the quantum harmonic oscillator. We obtain explicit formulas for their transition densities, fundamental solutions and Green functions. We also show that each such diffusion can be constructed from killed Brownian motion by a finite sequence of Darboux transformations followed by a Doob $h$-transform. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the connection polynomials in the generalized Mehler formula and use it to prove several conjectures concerning these polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Kuznetsov, Minjian Yuan

item.title: Common tiles from fractional tiles for two lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.31136v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $L_1, L_2\subseteq{\mathbb R}^d$ be lattices of the same volume and let $D_1, D_2$ be two bounded fundamental domains for $L_1, L_2$. We show that there is a measurable common tile for $L_1$ and $L_2$ contained in $D_1+D_2$. The main tool is a result of Bowen, Kun and Sabok (2021) which shows how to obtain a measurable perfect matching given a fractional perfect matching in hyperfinite graphings.
item.dc:creator: Jan Greb\'ik, Mihail N. Kolountzakis

item.title: Fourier inequalities and sign uncertainty
item.description: arXiv:2505.15994v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by inequalities in Fourier analysis, we present an improvement on the lower bound for the sign uncertainty principle of Bourgain, Clozel and Kahane in high dimensions. Additionally, our methods can be used to match the existing Torquato-Stillinger lower bounds for the Cohn-Elkies linear program for sphere packing.
item.dc:creator: Roni Edwin

item.title: Fourier Restriction Beyond Dimension Data: A Multiscale Moment Criterion
item.description: arXiv:2610.11227v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish an exact restriction criterion for weighted Moran measures with uniformly bounded one-level frame bounds: for every $2<s<\infty$, $L^2(\mu)\to L^s(\mathbb R)$ extension holds if and only if $\widehat\mu\in L^s(\mathbb R)$, equivalently, if and only if $\sum_nG_{s,n}<\infty$, where $G_{s,n}$ sums the $s$th powers of the magnitudes of the $n$th digit mask at its nonzero grid frequencies. The proof combines finite-frame stability and multiscale iteration with disjoint resonant frequency grids. The criterion determines the critical restriction exponent and characterizes its attainment when it lies in $(1,2)$. We construct singular continuous spectral Moran measures with common scales, digit cardinalities, exponential spectrum, maximal mask magnitudes at nonzero grid frequencies, and a global Fourier decay bound sharp along a common resonant sequence, yet different critical restriction exponents. For any prescribed finite positive summability exponent of these maxima, we determine the optimal interval of critical restriction exponents and realize both endpoint attainment and failure at every interior point with the same fixed data. These measures can simultaneously satisfy $\dim_{\mathrm F}^{\theta}\mu=\theta$ for $0\le\theta\le1$ and $D_q(\mu)=1$ for $1<q\le\infty$, with local dimension one at every support point. Finite-field spectral constructions realize every critical restriction exponent in $[1,2]$ with these dimensional data and exhibit sharp logarithmic endpoint transitions. They also yield singular continuous measures with Fourier dimension zero, restriction for all $1\le p<2$, and stretched-logarithmic Fourier decay with an optimal exponent. Finally, all-scale $L^q$-dimension formulas yield explicit examples where dimensional criteria strictly improve the classical Stein--Tomas--Mockenhaupt range.
item.dc:creator: Jinjun Li

item.title: Nearly Sharp Uniform Projection Bounds and Superlinear Vitushkin Inequalities for Deterministic Self-Similar Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.22908v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For all integers $1 \le k < d$ and every $\alpha \in (0,1)$, we construct an explicit deterministic finite homogeneous iterated function system of similarities in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space satisfying the open set condition. The same system is used at every scale. Its attractor $F_{k,\alpha}$ has positive and finite $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Write $A_\delta$ for the closed $\delta$-neighbourhood of a set $A$. For all sufficiently small $\delta > 0$, every orthogonal projection of $(F_{k,\alpha})_\delta$ onto a $k$-plane has $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure at most $C_{k,\alpha}(\log(1/\delta))^{-\alpha}$. The construction places the product of a planar self-similar set $E_\alpha$ and the unit $(k-1)$-cube in a coordinate $(k+1)$-plane. For every $0 < \delta < 1$, the supremum of these projected measures is comparable, up to constants depending only on $k$, to the supremum of the lengths of the orthogonal projections of $(E_\alpha)_\delta$ onto lines. We bound this latter supremum by $C_\alpha(\log(1/\delta))^{-\alpha}$ for all sufficiently small $\delta > 0$. We also prove that the analytic capacity $\gamma((E_\alpha)_\delta)$ is comparable to $(\log(1/\delta))^{-1/2}$ for all sufficiently small $\delta > 0$, with constants depending only on $\alpha$. Consequently, the Favard length of $(E_\alpha)_\delta$ is at most $C_\alpha\gamma((E_\alpha)_\delta)^{2\alpha}$ for every $0 < \delta < 1$. This quantitative Vitushkin inequality is superlinear for $\alpha > 1/2$, and its exponent $2\alpha$ approaches the optimal upper limit of two for this class of self-similar sets as $\alpha$ tends to one.
item.dc:creator: Kaining Jia, Layna Mangiapanello, Caleb Marshall, Victoria Risner

item.title: Riesz Transform Bounds Imply Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability of Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32534v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that if a $(k+2)$-Ahlfors--David regular measure $\mu$ in parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$ has support equal to a parabolic Lipschitz graph with sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(\mu)$, then $\mu$ is parabolic uniformly rectifiable and the graph is regular parabolic Lipschitz. The result holds for every integer $0\leq k\leq n-1$.
item.dc:creator: John Hoffman

item.title: Separating the Polar of Sets of Uniqueness from the Polars of All $H^{(d)}$-Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.02241v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a perfect set of uniqueness on the circle carrying a continuous probability measure which annihilates every $H^{(d)}$-set, simultaneously for all finite dimensions d. This gives a strict inclusion between the polar of the compact sets of uniqueness and the polar of the union of the classes $H^{(d)}$, answering a question raised in earlier work on these polars. The construction uses random binary increments of size comparable to the reciprocal of a product of square roots. A Gaussian sampling estimate gives a uniform Fourier-tail bound for all pseudomeasures supported by the resulting set, and also bounded atomic approximation and spectral synthesis. A separate energy estimate, stable under deletion of a small number of increments, yields full support for every limiting quasi-independent image of every positive measure absolutely continuous with respect to the constructed measure.
item.dc:creator: V\'aclav Vlas\'ak

item.title: Fourier inequalities and sign uncertainty II
item.description: arXiv:2611.08224v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Building on our earlier work, we present an $L^2$-$L^1$ inequality for radial Fourier eigenfunctions, relating this to the sign uncertainty principle of Bourgain, Clozel and Kahane. We also propose a generalisation of the aforementioned uncertainty principle, and draw a connection with entropic uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Roni Edwin

item.title: Fractional integration with singularity on the light-cone
item.description: arXiv:2611.20032v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we solve a classical problem investigated by Gelfand and Shilov on a family of fractional integral operators whose kernels have singularity appeared on the light-cone in R^n+1. As an implication, we obtain a desired sharp estimate for the L^p to L^q-boundedness of cone multiplier operators having a negative order.
item.dc:creator: Zipeng Wang

item.title: Polynomial spaces are locally Paley-Wiener: local spectral geometry, sampling, and interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2611.25844v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We identify the local Paley-Wiener structure of multivariate polynomial spaces on centrally symmetric convex bodies and apply it to sampling and interpolation. For a Bernstein-Markov measure with a positive continuous density in the interior, the normalized reproducing kernel at scale $1/n$ converges to the Fourier transform of the uniform probability measure on the dual unit ball of the Baran metric. We call this set the local spectral body. It describes the frequencies available to polynomials near each point. By recovering local bandlimited functions together with their $L^2$ norms, we obtain bulk universality and Christoffel asymptotics uniformly on compact subsets of the interior. This connection allows us to use Fourier methods to study polynomial sampling. If weighted sampling is uniformly stable with asymptotically one node per polynomial coefficient, almost every local spectral body must admit an exponential Riesz basis. Combining this result with Ortega-Cerd\`a's theorem for smooth spectra, we show that in dimension $d\ge2$, a $C^2$ boundary with everywhere positive curvature forces a positive proportion of extra sampling nodes. This rules out uniformly stable complete interpolation on such bodies. The same lower bound on the number of nodes applies to positive cubature exact through degree $2n$, since such a rule preserves the squared $L^2$ norm of every polynomial of degree at most $n$. The corresponding local-to-global problem remains open. If the local spectral body at every interior point admits an exponential Riesz basis, can one choose exactly as many nodes as polynomial coefficients at each degree so that sampling and interpolation are uniformly stable on the whole body?
item.dc:creator: Xinpeng Huang

item.title: Uniformly Expanding Coupled Maps: Self-Consistent Transfer Operators and Propagation of Chaos
item.description: arXiv:2209.13571v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation, uniformly in time, for systems of $N$ deterministic uniformly expanding heterogeneously coupled maps. The local dynamics and interactions may vary between coordinates, so exchangeability is not required. Under assumptions (independent of the dimension) on expansion, regularity, and weak-coupling, we construct self-consistent transfer operators whose product evolutions approximate every fixed finite marginal. For a class of weakly dependent initial laws (containing products), the error is $O(N^{-1})$ on fixed time intervals and $O(\log N/N)$ uniformly in time. The finite-time rate is optimal within this class. An explicit family exhibits error of order $\sqrt{\log N}/N$ at times of order $\log N$, proving that a uniform $O(N^{-1})$ bound is impossible in general; the optimal correction remains open. The proof is based on ergodic theory: expansion preserves classes of regular, weakly dependent densities, while transfer-operator contraction controls error accumulation. These classes yield concentration estimates and allow direct comparison of densities, giving strong propagation of chaos without external noise. Under additional assumptions, we also obtain Gaussian approximation for empirical observables on fixed time intervals and invariant neighbourhoods of stable fixed points of the self-consistent operator.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Ekstroem, Matteo Tanzi, Giuseppe Tenaglia

item.title: Mahler's problem and Turyn polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2405.08281v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mahler's problem asks for the largest possible value of the Mahler measure, normalized by the $L_2$ norm, of a polynomial with $\pm1$ coefficients and large degree. We establish a new record value of approximately $0.951$ in this problem by analyzing certain Turyn polynomials, which are defined by cyclically shifting the coefficients of a Fekete polynomial by a prescribed amount. Recently, Klurman, Lamzouri, and Munsch established that the distribution of values over the unit circle of Fekete polynomials of large degree is effectively modeled by a particular random point process. We extend this analysis to the Turyn polynomials, and determine expressions for the asymptotic normalized Mahler measure of these polynomials, as well as for their normalized $L_q$ norms. We also describe a number of calculations on the corresponding random processes, which indicate that the Turyn polynomials where the shift is approximately $1/4$ of the length have Mahler measure exceeding $95\%$ of their $L_2$ norm. Further, we show that these asymptotic values are not disturbed by a small change to make polynomials having entirely $\pm1$ coefficients, which establishes the result on Mahler's problem. We also estimate that the limiting value of the normalized $L_1$ norm of these polynomials exceeds $0.977$, in connection with a question of Newman.
item.dc:creator: Michael J. Mossinghoff

item.title: Fourier transform of nonlinear images of self-similar measures: quantitative aspects
item.description: arXiv:2503.07508v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper relates to the Fourier decay properties of images of self-similar measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^k$ under nonlinear smooth maps $f \colon \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}$. For example, we prove that if the linear parts of the similarities defining $\mu$ commute and the graph of $f$ has non-vanishing Gaussian curvature and $\kappa_2 > k/2$, then the Fourier dimension of the image measure is at least $\frac{2(2\kappa_2 - k)}{4 + 2\kappa_* - k}$, where $\kappa_2$ is the lower correlation dimension of $\mu$ and $\kappa_*$ is the Assouad dimension of the support of $\mu$. Under some additional assumptions on $\mu$, we use recent breakthroughs in the fractal uncertainty principle to obtain further improvements for the decay exponents. We give several applications to nonlinear arithmetic of self-similar sets $F$ in the line. For example, we prove that if $\dim_{\mathrm H} F > (\sqrt{65} - 5)/4 = 0.765\dots$ then the arithmetic product set $F \cdot F = \{ xy : x,y \in F \}$ has positive Lebesgue measure, while if $\dim_{\mathrm H} F > (-3 + \sqrt{41})/4 = 0.850\dots$ then $F \cdot F \cdot F$ has non-empty interior. One feature of the above results is that they do not require any separation conditions on the self-similar sets.
item.dc:creator: Amlan Banaji, Han Yu

item.title: Differential Equations for Macdonald's Hypergeometric Series
item.description: arXiv:2510.10875v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study differential equations for certain multivariable hypergeometric series, introduced by Macdonald in the 1980s, which generalize hypergeometric functions of matrix argument due to Bochner and Herz. Such equations are well studied in the one-variable case, where they serve to characterize the classical hypergeometric functions $_p F_q(z)$ and provide a route to many of their key properties. Accordingly, Macdonald asked for a similar characterization for the multivariate series. This problem, however, has remained open. Differential equations are known only for a handful of cases with $p\leq 3$ and $q\leq 2$. In this paper we give a complete solution to Macdonald's problem. In the multivariable case there are \emph{two} series $_p F_q(x)$ and $_p F_q(x,y)$, depending on $p+q+1$ parameters and one or two sets of variables, $x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ and $y=(y_1,\dots,y_n)$. We give differential equations characterizing both series, for all values of $p$ and $q$. The proof involves several new ideas in the theory of symmetric functions, especially Jack polynomials and interpolation polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Hong Chen, Siddhartha Sahi

item.title: Liouvillian integrability of vector fields in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2512.15522v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider complex rational vector fields in dimension $n>2$ (equivalently, differential forms of degree $n-1$ in $n$ variables) which admit a Liouvillian first integral. Extending a classical result by Singer for $n=2$, our main result states that there exists a first integral which is obtained by two successive integrations from one-forms with coefficients in a finite algebraic extension of the rational function field. The proof uses Puiseux series in a novel way to simplify computations. We also apply this method to give elementary proofs of Singer's theorem for rational one-forms, and of the Prelle-Singer theorem on elementary integrability of rational vector fields.
item.dc:creator: Waleed Aziz, Colin Christopher, Chara Pantazi, Sebastian Walcher

item.title: Algebraic Hodge generic points are dense
item.description: arXiv:2606.08882v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $f: X \to S$ be a quasi-projective family of varieties defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}} \subset \mathbb{C}$. We show that the points of $S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ that are Hodge generic for the variation of Hodge structures associated to $f$ are analytically dense in $S(\mathbb{C})$. In fact, in the spirit of the Grothendieck period conjecture and under a large monodromy assumption, we prove the density of the points of $S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ where the periods of the fibre do not satisfy extra relations 'up to degree $\delta$'. As a by-product, we also establish new instances of the Mumford-Tate conjecture, beyond the realm of abelian motives. When the base $S$ is a curve, we provide quantitative estimates for points satisfying these properties. The main technical contribution is a new result on relations satisfied by solutions of $G$-operators, which relies on height estimates due to Bombieri and Andr\'e.
item.dc:creator: Gregorio Baldi, Gal Binyamini, David Urbanik

item.title: On $H=W$ in Banach function spaces
item.description: arXiv:2606.19530v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we prove ``$H=W$" in the context of a Banach function space $X(\Omega)$. Let $\Omega$ be a subset of ${\mathbb R}^n$ and denote by $W^1_X(\Omega)$ the collection of all those $f\in X(\Omega)$ whose distributional derivatives $\partial_jf$ are contained in $X(\Omega)$. Our main result provides a small collection of ``universal" hypotheses on $X(\Omega)$ that ensure $W^1_X(\Omega)$ is equal to $H^1_X(\Omega)$, the formal closure of ${Lip}(\Omega)\cap W^1_X(\Omega)$ with respect to the norm \[\|f\|_{W^1_X(\Omega)} = \|f\|_{X(\Omega)} + \|\nabla f\|_{X(\Omega)}.\] The main theorem has two corollaries. The first gives a slightly stronger set of hypotheses for ``$H=W$", and the second gives density of $C^\infty_c({\mathbb R}^n)$ in $W^1_X({\mathbb R}^n)$.
item.dc:creator: \c{S}eyma \c{C}etin, David Cruz-Uribe, Scott Rodney

item.title: Harmonic weights in inverse central binomial series
item.description: arXiv:2607.09904v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study how the partial fraction coefficients of an inverse central binomial series change when the harmonic weight $H_{pn}$ is replaced by $H_{qn}$. For positive integers $p<q$, every coefficient increases. As the index $k$ grows, the increase tends to $2\log(q/p)$ uniformly over all angles $0<\phi\le\pi$, even when the angle approaches either endpoint. The increase is above the limit at every odd index and below it at every even index. We give the first correction, of order $k^{-2/q}$ for $q>2$ and of order $k^{-2}$ for $(p,q)=(1,2)$. For the normalized transforms, subtracting $c$ times the first from the second gives a Stieltjes function exactly when $c\le1$. We also determine which real dilations $0<p<q$ satisfy the same sign law. For $p\ge1$ it holds exactly when $q\ge2$. For $0<p<1$ it holds above a threshold $Q(p)$, and at the threshold it holds precisely on one interval $0<p<p_*$. Finally, we give angle identities at every odd weight from three onward and determine which Dirichlet $L$-terms cancel at angle $\pi/3$.
item.dc:creator: K. Srinivasa Raghava

item.title: Differential inclusions and the chattering phenomenon
item.description: arXiv:2610.03561v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This is a second draft of a manuscript about existence of solutions of differential inclusions involving chattering.
item.dc:creator: Martin Ivanov

item.title: Constructions and reductions on the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23785v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate five open problems concerning the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations posed by Marinescu and Niculescu. We give constructive answers to three of them. First, we construct an equivalent norm on $\ell^2$ with no three-dimensional Hornich-Hlawka subspace. Second, we present a Nakano space that is not Hornich-Hlawka. Third, we show that the $\alpha$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality fails to hold on nonzero normed spaces when $\alpha \in (1, 2) \cup (2, \infty)$. This implies that on every nonzero inner product space, the $\alpha$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality holds for all triples precisely when $\alpha \in (0,1] \cup \{2\}$. For the remaining two problems, we establish reductions. We prove that $\ell^p(N)$ is Hornich-Hlawka for all $N \geq 3$ and $2 < p \leq \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$ if and only if it is Hornich-Hlawka at $N = 3$ and $p = \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$. Finally, for $p(\cdot): (0, 1) \to [1, 2]$ measurable and integers $k \geq 0$, we establish a Sobolev-Nakano equivalence: we prove that $W^{k,p(\cdot)}(0,1)$, equipped with the sum of the Luxemburg norms of its derivatives of orders $0, \ldots, k$, is Hornich-Hlawka if and only if $L^{p(\cdot)}(0,1)$ is Hornich-Hlawka.
item.dc:creator: Seokbin Lee

item.title: Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms
item.description: arXiv:2611.02886v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Auscher (LMO)
